children: provided a guidance update as part of its presentation at the Barclays Global Consumer Staples Conference.
The company expects to report third-quarter total company adjusted operating income in the range of $115M to $175M. By segment, Smithfield Foods

expects to report a fresh pork third-quarter adjusted operating loss in the range of $70M to $90M, primarily driven by industry spread compression. The company now expects to report hog production third-quarter adjusted operating profit in the range of $25M to $45M, primarily driven by lower hog prices. For the packaged meat segment, the company reaffirmed its outlook for FY26 adjusted operating income of between $1,075M and $1,150M, unchanged from the prior range, reflecting continued branded volume share gains, expanded distribution, and disciplined execution in a cautious consumer environment.

"Our most important business segment, packaged meats, continues to perform well, gaining branded share and expanding distribution even as consumers remain cautious," highlighted CEO Shane Smith. "The change in our outlook is driven by external market conditions within portions of the pork value chain. While we are disappointed in how these commodity market dynamics will impact our near-term results, we remain focused on executing our strategies, maintaining operational discipline, and relying on our strong balance sheet to manage through this environment and continue investing in long-term growth," he added.
